item.title: [ecmascript] for await (… of …) and Array.fromAsync now close rejecting sync iterables
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/fromAsync

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/for-await...of

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

No error handling for sync iterables

Iterating over sync iterables and generators

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

After tc39/ecma262#2600 was merged into the JavaScript specification, both for await (… of …) and Array.fromAsync(…) now close sync iterables when they yield rejected promises.

In other words:

  • When a sync generator yields a rejected promise within a try block,
  • And then the async generator creates an iterable that is fed into for await (… of …) or Array.fromAsync(…),
  • Then the sync generator’s finally block used to not be evaluated,
  • But, after tc39/ecma262#2600, now the finally block will be evaluated.

I believe V8 already has deployed this change.

What did you expect to see?

In the Array.fromAsync article:

  • The “No error handling for sync iterables” heading should be renamed “Error handling for sync iterables”.
  • The text:
    “Similar to for await...of, if the object being iterated is a sync iterable, and an error is thrown while iterating, the return() method of the underlying iterator will not be called, so the iterator is not closed”
    should be changed to:
    “Similar to for await...of, if the object being iterated is a sync iterable, and an error is thrown while iterating, the return() method of the underlying iterator will be called, and the iterator will be closed”.
  • The code block with function* generatorWithRejectedPromises should be tweaked to indicate that the called finally message is printed.
  • Everything in the section starting from “If you need to close the iterator, you need to use a for...of loop instead” should be removed.

In the for await...of article:

  • In the “Iterating over sync iterables and generators, everything starting from “Note: Be aware of yielding rejected promises from a sync generator” should be edited similarly to the Array.fromAsync changes.
  • As for Array.fromAsync, the code block with function* generatorWithRejectedPromises should be tweaked to indicate that the called finally message is printed.
  • As for Array.fromAsync, everything in the section starting from “To make finally blocks of a sync generator always called, use the appropriate form of the loop” should be removed.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

  • tc39/ecma262#2600
  • tc39/test262#4450
  • tc39/proposal-array-from-async#49

Do you have anything more you want to share?

No response

item.title: [ecmascript] Yielding rejected promises from a sync generator now properly closes the iterator
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/for-await...of

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

From Note: until but not including Specification.

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

It seems at least modern Chrome does correctly call finally in the specified circumstances.

Assuming this is the case in all modern browsers and is perhaps even specified as such,
the corresponding content should be removed.

What did you expect to see?

No warning about an obsolete issue, assuming it actually is.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

Someone should check what the relevant spec says, I'm too busy, sorry.

item.title: [streams, ecmascript] ReadableStreamDefaultController: undocumented error conditions
item.content:encoded:
MDN URL

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/ReadableStreamDefaultController/close

What specific section or headline is this issue about?

Exceptions

What information was incorrect, unhelpful, or incomplete?

The "Exceptions" section says:

TypeError
Thrown if the source object is not a ReadableStreamDefaultController.

This suggests that errors are not thrown in other cases.

What did you expect to see?

I expect to see that a TypeError may be thrown by this method if the stream is already in the process of closing or closed.

Do you have any supporting links, references, or citations?

https://streams.spec.whatwg.org/#rs-default-controller-close

Do you have anything more you want to share?

Similar issues exist for ReadableStreamDefaultController.enqueue and probably methods on WritableStreamDefaultController as well.
